cards.text: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, has been warning Israel that judgment is coming, in the days of Jeroboam, king of Israel (Amos 1:1; Amos 1-6). Now he tells what the Lord GOD showed him. In the first vision, the Lord is preparing something just after the king's harvest, right as the late spring crop is coming up.

cards.question: In Amos's first vision, what is the Lord preparing as the late spring crop comes up?

cards.text: The locusts eat every green plant in the land. Like a tray of cookies in the break room at work: you turn around ONE time and it's just crumbs.

cards.question: With every green plant gone, Amos cries out and asks the Lord GOD to forgive.
Amos asks, "How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" Who is Amos worried about?
After Amos prays, the LORD tells him the locust plan will still go ahead.

cards.text: Second vision: the Lord GOD is calling for judgment by fire. Friend, the only fire I want near me is my oven at 350, and even THAT I peek at every two minutes.

cards.question: In Amos's second vision, the fire burns only a small corner of the land.
The fire consumes the great deep and devours the land. What does Amos do?

answers.text: He begs the Lord GOD to stop
He runs back home to Tekoa
He waits for the fire to pass

cards.question: Amos has pleaded about the fire. What does the Lord GOD say about it?

answers.text: It will burn for seven days

cards.text: Third vision, and it's quieter. The Lord is standing by a wall true to plumb, with a plumb line in His hand.
The LORD asks, "Amos, what do you see?" and Amos answers: a plumb line. Friend, if God asked ME that, I'd be sweating, sure it was a TRICK question.

cards.question: In Amos's third vision, where does the Lord say He is setting the plumb line?
Once the plumb line is set, Amos pleads again and the LORD relents a third time.

cards.text: Then the Lord names exactly what's coming, starting with Israel's places of worship.

cards.question: First on the Lord's list: the high places of Isaac will be ___.
The sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste too. Last, the Lord names a king's family. He says He will rise up with His sword against the house of ___.

cards.text: So the Lord's sword is pointed right at the king's own house.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but its two wrong answers are invented groups rather than real details from somewhere in the Bible. Amos's own family in Tekoa and the king's harvest workers are not biblical details supplied as alternatives here.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish. Wrong answers for what someone does or says only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The decisive turn in Amos 7:8 is left unclear. Marking this compound statement false does not establish whether Amos does not plead again, whether the LORD does not relent, or both. No other card clearly tells the Lord's actual announcement that He will no longer spare Israel.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card merely restates card 17's answered detail about the sword coming against Jeroboam's house. It adds no new moment and functions as a recap rather than moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.
